paper_summary: MS thesis (University of Oklahoma, 2025) on Direct Ink Writing (DIW) 3D printing of epoxy syntactic foams. EPON 815C / Epikure 3230 epoxy was filled with 3M hollow glass microballoons (S60, iM16K, iM30K) at 40 wt% relative to epoxy weight, with 1 wt% fumed silica and a thixotropic additive paste to give shear-thinning, yield-stress inks; specimens were printed with a 410 um nozzle at 10 mm/s and cured 2 h at 80 C plus 3 h at 125 C. Cast and printed tensile (0/45/90 deg) and compression (uni- and bi-directional, X/Y) specimens were tested at 1 mm/min: printed parts were more consistent than cast ones, iM30K gave the best tensile properties, S60 the highest compressive modulus, and hybrid iM30K:iM16K inks (1:3, 2:2, 3:1) were used to optimise specific properties, with iM30K_2 iM16K_2 best overall (highest specific strength/modulus, MCF 1551 N, PCF 2103 N). The optimum hybrid ink was printed into 30% infill hexagonal honeycomb cores whose in-plane compression showed higher peak strength in the Y-direction (9.423 MPa) and higher modulus in the X-direction (0.236 GPa).

extraction_notes:
MS thesis; the whole document (84 pages) was read, including Tables 1-3 and the reference list. Most quantitative results live in figures (Figs. 9, 11-13, 15-17, 19-24, 27) whose individual bar values are not tabulated, so only values stated explicitly in the running text or in the three tables were extracted; everything else was left null rather than read off plots.

Unit conversions: tensile/compressive moduli GPa -> MPa (x1000). Specific properties converted from GPa/(kg/m3) or MPa/(kg/m3) to the schema's MPa per g/cm3 by multiplying by 1e6 or 1e3 respectively: cast iM30K specific tensile modulus 8.88e-4 GPa/(kg/m3) -> 888 MPa/(g/cc) and specific tensile strength 4.42e-2 MPa/(kg/m3) -> 44.2 MPa/(g/cc); hybrid 2:2 compressive specific strength 0.081 MPa/(kg/m3) -> 81 MPa/(g/cc) and specific modulus 4.24e-4 GPa/(kg/m3) -> 424 MPa/(g/cc); honeycomb X 0.00051 GPa/(kg/m3) -> 510 and 0.0130 MPa/(kg/m3) -> 13.0; honeycomb Y 0.00042 -> 420 and 0.0232 -> 23.2 (Sec. 4.4 restates these as 0.00052 and 0.00041; the Sec. 4.3 values were used). Energy absorption for the 1:3 hybrid was converted from the reported SEA of 41.393 J/g using the paper's own measured density of 0.635 g/cm3, giving 26.28 MJ/m3; the raw EA (4.360 J) and MCF/PCF forces have no schema field and are recorded in specimen_notes.

Particle wall_thickness_ratio (eta = inner/outer radius) was computed from Table 1 mean diameter and wall thickness: S60 (15-1.49)/15 = 0.901, iM16K (10-0.72)/10 = 0.928, iM30K (7.65-0.70)/7.65 = 0.908. Particle loading is reported only as '40 wt% relative to the weight of epoxy', i.e. 40 parts per 100 parts resin, not a weight fraction of the whole composite, so particle_weight_fraction was left null and the loading recorded in additional_fillers; no particle volume fractions are given anywhere in the thesis (only qualitative statements that iM16K gives the highest and iM30K the lowest volume fraction at fixed weight fraction).

Caveats: (1) Table 3 (area-corrected strengths, 42.33/38.00/40.23 MPa as-measured and 73.23/68.78/96.55 MPa corrected for 0/45/90 deg) does not state which base ink the 'example specimen' came from; it appears in the base-ink section immediately after the iM30K SEM discussion, so iM30K was assumed - confidence lowered to 0.5 for those three records. (2) The hybrid tensile strengths 42.45 and 37.70 MPa are stated in the same sentence that names the 90 deg orientation only for the 43.05 MPa value; the 90 deg attribution for the other two is inferred (confidence 0.6). (3) The specific compressive modulus 0.000424 GPa/(kg/m3) is the top of a stated range and was attributed to the 2:2 hybrid on the basis of the Chapter 5 statement that it had the highest specific modulus. (4) The reported 2:2 compressive specific strength (0.081 MPa/(kg/m3) x 0.735 g/cm3 implies ~59 MPa) sits above the text's statement that printed peak compressive strengths 'remained below 50 MPa' for the base inks; both are reported as-is. (5) Base-ink compression results are given mostly as ranges (modulus 0.236-0.590 GPa for iM16K/iM30K, peak strength 28.68-49.21 MPa across all inks, strain at peak 0.104-0.245 mm/mm) without per-configuration attribution, so only the S60 Bi-X modulus of 0.619 GPa could be recorded; the S60 minimum strain at peak of 0.104 and the iM16K/iM30K maximum of 0.245 are noted here but not assigned to records. (6) Cast compression is described only as 'certain cast specimens reached compressive strengths exceeding 60 MPa' - no record created. (7) Rheology results (Herschel-Bulkley tau0 = 67.56 / 93.32 / 200.00 Pa and wall shear stress 497.87 / 448.11 / 853.23 Pa for S60 / iM16K / iM30K in Table 2; amplitude-sweep dynamic yield stresses 75.016 / 71.561 / 43.420 Pa) have no schema field and are not recorded as properties. (8) Test temperature is not stated; 25 C was used because all printing and testing was done under ambient laboratory conditions. Crosshead rate was 1 mm/min for all tests but specimen gauge lengths/heights are not given, so no strain rate could be computed. (9) Cure was 2 h at 80 C then 3 h at 125 C; 125 C recorded as the process temperature. (10) The honeycomb records describe an architected 30% infill structure, not a bulk foam, so their moduli/strengths are structural rather than material properties.
